model_scope: Frozen EXPOSURE, ORIGINAL versus EDGE_FLIP; no training outputs included
image_regions_viewed: Each output's az=-60 and az=120 oblique views plus the unchanged front and side section locations
limitations: Labels are visible and the reviewer has prior high-level context about this parent; this is not a blinded assessment.
No metric tables or previous label files were consulted to assign these image-based ratings.
A plausible seating role does not certify shared vertex IDs, watertightness, legal interfaces or load-bearing contact.
A short or interrupted line in a fixed section is not sufficient evidence of a disconnected mesh fragment or a crack.
The displayed mesh is small within the sheet; fine connectivity and hidden contacts remain uncertain.
No unique source style is required; changes of reasonable bench design are not failures by themselves.

In the fixed front section its long blue line is around y=0.24, while the prominent gray horizontal structure and tops of the sectioned legs are around y=0.0. The second oblique view also shows a gray level below the blue surface. This leaves the blue surface's actual support/contact unresolved; the lower gray level could be underframe geometry, and the images do not establish that it is an illegal duplicate seat. The side section has several separated short line segments, but the oblique views do not establish detached fragments from those segments.

EDGE_FLIP.observations: The same long bench, broad end supports and elevated back rail remain visible in both oblique views. Blue C remains at the same apparent seat position. The front section retains the visible vertical separation between blue C and the lower gray horizontal level; the side section retains local short or interrupted segments. There are small line-position differences, but no clear loss of a major support or newly resolved C-contact relationship is visible. Neither connectivity nor a distinct floating fragment is established by these section segments.

paired_judgment.notes: The flip preserves the main organization. It does not visibly resolve the existing height/contact ambiguity of blue C, and no robust quality gain or clear new failure is identifiable from these views.
